title_en: Wang Lianshun v. China Life Insurance Company, Yongshun County Branch — insurance contract dispute

full_text_en:
Wang Lianshun v. China Life Insurance Company, Yongshun County Branch

Dispute over Insurance Contract

Plaintiff: Wang Lianshun, male, 49 years old, cadre, residing at the dormitory of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Yongshun County, Hunan Province.

Defendant: China Life Insurance Company, Yongshun County Branch of Hunan Province. Domicile: Yongshun County Town, Hunan Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Chunyan, Manager of the Company.

Agents ad litem: Yang Songpo, Deputy Manager of China Life Insurance Company, Yongshun County Branch of Hunan Province.

Agent ad litem: Deng Xingping, lawyer of Hunan Sanye Law Firm.

Chen Xiaolan, the wife of the plaintiff Wang Lianshun, brought a lawsuit before the Yongshun County People's Court of Hunan Province against the defendant China Life Insurance Company, Yongshun County Branch of Hunan Province (hereinafter referred to as Yongshun Life Insurance) over a dispute concerning an insurance contract. During the litigation, Chen Xiaolan died of illness, and Wang Lianshun continued the lawsuit on behalf of this case.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The defendant's entity had previously purchased gynecological cancer screening insurance for my wife, Chen Xiaolan, who worked there, with a policy term of three years and a premium of RMB 10,000. After my wife contracted cancer during the policy period, the defendant refused to settle the claim. We request the court to order the defendant to pay the insurance benefits in accordance with the insurance contract, and to compensate for the mental distress suffered by my wife before her death due to the defendant's refusal to settle the claim.

Defendant's Defense: It is true that our entity purchased gynecological cancer screening insurance for female employees for the benefit of our own staff. However, because Chen Xiaolan was later transferred out of our entity, we no longer had an insurable interest, and therefore we terminated the insurance contract by means of a business endorsement. Since the insurance contract no longer exists, the plaintiff's claim for insurance benefits is naturally invalid. The plaintiff's claim should be dismissed.

The Yongshun County People's Court of Hunan Province found the following facts upon trial:

On October 30, 1995, the former People's Insurance Company of China, Yongshun County Branch, purchased gynecological cancer screening insurance for six female employees of the entity (including Chen Xiaolan, wife of plaintiff Wang Lianshun), under policy number 95-018. The policyholder and the insurer were both the Yongshun County Insurance Company, and the insureds and beneficiaries were these six female employees. The policy term was three years, the sum insured was RMB 10,000, and the premium was RMB 40 per person. The premium was paid in a lump sum from the trade union funds of the Yongshun County Insurance Company.

In June 1996, the former People's Insurance Company of China, Yongshun County Branch, was split into two entities: a life insurance company and a property insurance company. Chen Xiaolan was assigned to work at the defendant, Yongshun Life Insurance. In July 1997, Chen Xiaolan was transferred from Yongshun Life Insurance to work at the Jishou Branch of Ping An Insurance Company of China. On August 5 of the same year, Yongshun Life Insurance issued a business endorsement, terminating the insurance contract on the ground that Chen Xiaolan no longer had an insurable interest, without notifying Chen Xiaolan in writing. In January 1998, the Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture People's Hospital of Hunan Province diagnosed Chen Xiaolan with cancer, which was later confirmed as endometrial adenocarcinoma by the Hunan Cancer Hospital. After contracting cancer, Chen Xiaolan submitted applications for insurance benefits to Yongshun Life Insurance twice, in January and May 1998. On July 21 of the same year, Yongshun Life Insurance issued a notice of refusal to pay insurance benefits to Chen Xiaolan, on the ground that she no longer had an insurable interest after her transfer and that the insurance contract had lapsed. For this reason, Chen Xiaolan filed a lawsuit on February 8, 1999, and died on July 8 of the same year due to the worsening of her cancer.

The Yongshun County People's Court of Hunan Province held the following opinion:

Any entity seeking lawful benefits for its own employees is a proper act permitted and supported by law. Since insurance was the business of the former People's Insurance Company of China, Yongshun County Branch, and this insurance was purchased by the company for its own employees, this special circumstance resulted in the policyholder and the insurer signing the same insurance contract. However, this is different from a void contract signed by oneself with oneself; it still constitutes a contract entered into between two equal civil subjects. Based on the actual circumstances of the premium contribution, it should be determined that the policyholder of this insurance contract was the trade union of the former People's Insurance Company of China, Yongshun County Branch, and the insurer was the company itself. Protecting the lawful rights and interests of employees, caring for their lives, and serving them wholeheartedly are the functions of the trade union. The trade union's purchase of personal insurance for employees with their consent is a manifestation of its performance of duties. In accordance with the provisions of Article 52, paragraph 2 of the Insurance Law of the PRC, the trade union of the former People's Insurance Company of China, Yongshun County Branch, had an insurable interest in the subject matter of the insurance. In accordance with Article 12 of the Insurance Law, the personal insurance contract in this case represents the true intent of the parties, was lawfully established, and is valid.

Chen Xiaolan, the wife of plaintiff Wang Lianshun, while working at the former People's Insurance Company of China, Yongshun County Branch, was both an employee of that company and a member of its trade union, and was entitled to the benefits of employees and members. The former People's Insurance Company of China, Yongshun County Branch, using the trade union's funds to purchase insurance for its female employees, constituted a welfare benefit provided by the company's trade union for its members. By virtue of the establishment of the insurance contract, Chen Xiaolan became a party to the contract in her capacity as the insured and beneficiary. In accordance with the provisions of Article 21, paragraphs 2 and 3 of the Insurance Law, Chen Xiaolan had the right to claim insurance benefits.

Under ordinary contracts, since they are based on the mutual agreement of the contracting parties, they can be modified or terminated as long as the parties agree. However, in insurance contracts, because the insured is involved and the contract is closely related to the insured's interests, the conclusion, modification, or termination of the contract can only be decided after notifying and soliciting the opinion of the insured. After Chen Xiaolan, the wife of plaintiff Wang Lianshun, was transferred out of the defendant, Yongshun Life Insurance, Yongshun Life Insurance took advantage of the convenience that the personal insurance contract was signed by the same person and terminated the contract in the form of a business endorsement without soliciting Chen Xiaolan's opinion. This act violated the provisions of Article 15 of the Insurance Law and cannot have the effect of termination.

Personnel mobility is a normal phenomenon in social development. For personal insurance contracts where the subject matter of insurance is the body of a mobile person, the insurable interest that the policyholder has in the subject matter at the time of coverage may change after coverage due to personnel mobility. For personal insurance contracts, the validity of the contract should only be determined based on whether the policyholder had an insurable interest at the time of coverage, and should not be determined based on personnel changes occurring after the contract is established. This is necessary to maintain the stability of the contract. The defendant, Yongshun Life Insurance, argued that after Chen Xiaolan was transferred out, Yongshun Life Insurance no longer had an insurable interest, and therefore the contract was invalid. This argument cannot be sustained.

A lawfully established contract is binding on all parties, and each party must enjoy rights and perform obligations in accordance with the contract. Chen Xiaolan, the wife of plaintiff Wang Lianshun, contracted gynecological cancer during the policy period, which met the coverage conditions stipulated in the insurance contract. The defendant, Yongshun Life Insurance, upon receiving the claim for insurance benefits, should have paid the insurance benefits as agreed. Wang Lianshun's claim for an order requiring Yongshun Life Insurance to pay insurance benefits should be supported. The claim for an order requiring Yongshun Life Insurance to compensate for Chen Xiaolan's mental distress, due to the lack of corresponding evidence, is not supported. Accordingly, the Yongshun County People's Court of Hunan Province rendered the following judgment on August 11, 1999:

1. The defendant, Yongshun Life Insurance, shall pay plaintiff Wang Lianshun insurance benefits in the amount of RMB 10,000;

2. The plaintiff Wang Lianshun's claim for compensation for mental distress from the defendant, Yongshun Life Insurance, is not supported.

Litigation costs of RMB 530 shall be borne by the defendant, Yongshun Life Insurance.

After the first-instance judgment became legally effective, the Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture People's Procuratorate of Hunan Province lodged a protest. The grounds were: the premium in this case was actually disbursed by the former People's Insurance Company of China, Yongshun County Branch, and the first-instance judgment's finding that it was disbursed from the trade union funds of that company lacked sufficient evidence, constituting an error in fact finding; Chen Xiaolan was not a party to the insurance contract, and after her transfer out of Yongshun Life Insurance, Yongshun Life Insurance lost its insurable interest, yet the first-instance judgment still held the contract valid, which was an improper application of law. The Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture Intermediate People's Court of Hunan Province instructed the Yongshun County People's Court of Hunan Province to retry the case.

The Yongshun County People's Court of Hunan Province formed a new collegial panel and, in accordance with first-instance procedures, found the following upon retrial:

The original judgment found that the premium in this case was disbursed from the trade union funds of the former People's Insurance Company of China, Yongshun County Branch. This was supported by a certificate issued by Hu Chunhua, the handler of the insurance business, in the name of the former People's Insurance Company of China, Yongshun County Branch. Although the certificate had formal defects, the facts it certified were certain. Furthermore, an examination of the accounting vouchers for the administrative and operational funds of the former People's Insurance Company of China, Yongshun County Branch, showed that from October 1 to October 30, 1995, there was no voucher in the accounts for the payment of premiums for the six female employees, including Chen Xiaolan.

The Yongshun County People's Court of Hunan Province held in the retrial that the protesting authority, alleging that the premium was disbursed by the former People's Insurance Company of China, Yongshun County Branch, did not provide any evidence. The argument that after Chen Xiaolan's transfer, the insurance contract became invalid because the policyholder lost its insurable interest cannot be sustained. The original judgment had clear findings of fact, reliable evidence, correct application of law, appropriate decision, and lawful trial procedures, and should be upheld. Accordingly, the court rendered the following judgment on May 16, 2000:

The protest is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

Litigation costs of RMB 930 shall be borne by the defendant at first instance, Yongshun Life Insurance.

After the judgment was pronounced, Yongshun Life Insurance, still dissatisfied, appealed to the Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture Intermediate People's Court of Hunan Province. The grounds of appeal were: 1. In the contract of this case, the appellant acted as both policyholder and insurer, and after consultation, modified part of the contract's content by issuing a business endorsement terminating the insurance liability for Chen Xiaolan. This was a lawful civil act. 2. Even if terminating the insurance liability for Chen Xiaolan by way of endorsement was invalid, since Chen Xiaolan had been transferred out, the appellant no longer had an insurable interest, and the part of the insurance contract concerning Chen Xiaolan should also be deemed invalid.

After second-instance trial, the Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture Intermediate People's Court of Hunan Province held the following:

The finding that the insurance contract in this case could not be terminated is not solely because it was terminated by an invalid endorsement, but more importantly because the termination was carried out without notifying Chen Xiaolan and soliciting her opinion. Although Chen Xiaolan was not a signatory to the insurance contract, as the insured and beneficiary of a personal insurance contract, she had the right to know the validity of the contract. In the absence of any notification, she had reason to believe that the insurance contract still existed. When she contracted cancer and applied for insurance benefits on that basis, the appellant, Yongshun Life Insurance, only then produced the endorsement terminating the contract. This act violated the principle of good faith that civil acts should follow and is certainly invalid.

Only agreements entered into by two or more equal civil subjects for the purpose of establishing, modifying, or terminating civil rights and obligations can be called contracts. The insurance contract in this case could be established precisely because one party was the insurer, the former People's Insurance Company of China, Yongshun County Branch, engaged in insurance business, and the other party was the trade union of the former People's Insurance Company of China, Yongshun County Branch, representing the interests of the six female employees. The appellant, Yongshun Life Insurance, while still involving the rights and interests of the other five female employees, neither wishes to deny the validity of the insurance contract in this case, nor can it claim that the insurance contract was signed by itself alone. This is not only inconsistent with the facts but also contrary to legal principles and is self-contradictory. If it were truly a "contract" signed by oneself with oneself, how could there be talk of "consultation and agreement" to modify the insurance contract? The grounds of Yongshun Life Insurance's appeal cannot be sustained. The original judgment is correct and should be affirmed. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the court rendered the following judgment on October 16, 2000:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

Case acceptance fee of RMB 400 shall be borne by the appellant, Yongshun Life Insurance.
